A 76-year-old male arrives at the emergency department following a near-syncopal episode while
working in his garage. His initial vital signs show: - Temperature: 98.8°F (37.1°C) - Blood pressure:
125/62 mmHg - Pulse: 117/min - Respirations: 14/min - O2 saturation: 98% on room air Laboratory
results reveal: - Hemoglobin: 7 g/dL - Hematocrit: 22% - Leukocyte count: 6,500/mm^3 with normal
differential - Platelet count: 197,000/mm^3 After initiating blood products and ordering a CT scan, the
patient's condition changes: - Temperature rises to 99.5°F (37.5°C) - Blood pressure drops to 87/48
mmHg - Pulse increases to 180/min - Patient develops labored breathing Which additional finding
would you most likely expect in this patient? Answer Choices: (A) An underlying malignancy causing
anemia of chronic disease (B) Sudden rupture of a vessel (C) Sepsis secondary to bacterial
contamination of transfused blood products (D) An undiagnosed bleeding disorder such as hemophilia
(E) Acute hemolysis due to ABO incompatibility (F) Hypocalcemia due to citrate toxicity from
transfusion (G) Autoimmune reaction against red blood cell antigens (H) Transfusion-associated
circulatory overload (TACO) (I) A past medical history of repeat GI and respiratory infections (J) A
history of chronic kidney disease causing erythropoietin deficiency
 A. Transfusion-associated circulatory overload (TACO)
B. Sepsis secondary to bacterial contamination of transfused blood products
C. A past medical history of repeat GI and respiratory infections
D. Acute hemolysis due to ABO incompatibility
E. An underlying malignancy causing anemia of chronic disease
F. Autoimmune reaction against red blood cell antigens
G. Hypocalcemia due to citrate toxicity from transfusion
H. An undiagnosed bleeding disorder such as hemophilia
I. Sudden rupture of a vessel

J. A history of chronic kidney disease causing erythropoietin deficiency
